summary: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon under Bryce Ryan, Cornell University, and Harvard University. He held posts at the University of Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and Harvard.

Stanley Lombardo works in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and he served on the faculty at the University of Kansas from circa 1976 to 2014.

Stanley Weinstein specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kodo Sawaki and Gyokusen Hosaka, the University of Tokyo, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at Komazawa, SOAS, London, and Yale.

Stanley Wolpert was an indology and history scholar. He studied at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, becoming an associate professor in 1963 and department chair in 1967.
Stefan Anacker was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison circa 1965–1970, where he studied under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums works in Buddhist studies, indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Washington, and held posts at the University of Copenhagen, University of Washington, University of Munich, Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of tibetology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Stockholm University under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm. He has held positions at UC Berkeley, the University of Virginia, and the University of Gävle.

Stefan Mario Maul is an archaeologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and Freie Universität Berlin. He held posts at Freie Universität Berlin, Heidelberg University as Ordinarius for Assyriology from 1995, and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She served as an assistant professor at the University of Groningen from circa 2012 to 2020 and held a post at SOAS University of London starting in 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Venice, Sichuan, and Leiden. He taught at Padua, Ca' Foscari University, and Soka University, and served as Yehan Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Oxford (2012–2020).

Steffen Döll specializes in Buddhist studies and japanology. He studied at the University of Munich and Kyoto University. His appointments include positions at Munich, Seikei University, and the University of Hamburg, where he became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism in 2015.

Stella Kramrisch was an indology and art history scholar. She completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. She held appointments at Visva-Bharati University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1993).

Sten Konow was a scholar of indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Oslo, Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, and Berlin. His main posts were at the Archaeological Survey of India, Hamburg, and Oslo.

Stephan Licha is a scholar of Buddhist studies and japanology who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London. He held postdoctoral positions at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, and is attested on the faculty at the University of Chicago.

Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia, where his teachers included Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer is a Buddhist studies and tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1971 to 1980 and worked at Sidley Austin.

Stephanie Kaza works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Oberlin College, Stanford University, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry, studying under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy. She was a professor at the University of Vermont.
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an indologist and linguist. She completed her doctoral work at Yale University under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She taught at Harvard University and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA circa 2002.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan, and held professorships at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (1992–2013).
